title: Mass Assignment and Parameter Type Confusion
platform_conditions: Ruby 3.x; MRI — request params are nested Hash/Array structures whose keys, nesting depth and value types the client controls
security_mechanism: HTTP parameters arrive as nested hashes with attacker-chosen keys and value types, but Ruby method signatures say nothing about either: code written for params[:user] as a flat hash of strings silently accepts user[role]=admin, or a Hash/Array where a String was expected, because assignment interfaces copy whatever keys they are handed into model attributes or query conditions. Without an explicit permit list, the caller sets any attribute — role, admin, approved — and condition interfaces fed raw nested params change query shape based on the value's runtime type.

source_sink_clues.source: Form and query bodies with attacker-controlled keys and nesting (user[role]=admin, key[]=...), including JSON request bodies.
source_sink_clues.sink: Model update interfaces fed the raw params hash (update(params[:user]), attributes=), and query condition interfaces receiving raw nested params values

tracking_guards: Require an explicit permit list between the request and the model (params.require(...).permit(:name, :email) style whitelisting); require type checks on params values (is_a?(String), to_s) before they enter comparisons or conditions.
not_candidate_when: Only permit-listed scalar keys reach the attribute update, params values are type-validated before use in conditions, or the hash is constructed server-side from known fields.
public_references: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/915.html
OWASP Web Application Security: Mass Assignment cheat sheet family — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Mass_Assignment_Cheat_Sheet.html
